## Short version

The three passages are rewritten below. Eleven project terms have no definition in the passages, and I could not define them. They are listed at the end, together with the definitions I added that you should verify.

## Passage 1

- **Block save.** A block holds 16 tokens. A run is up to 16 consecutive tokens inside one block. The block save transposes the K rows of a run in registers. It then writes them as whole 64-byte cache lines, with one store instruction per line. When the run does not fill the block, the store is masked (it writes only the part of the line that belongs to the run). Every decode step produces a run of one token. A run of one token still uses the scatter (a store that writes each value to its own address).
- **Sharing.** The main thread and the idle main helper threads share the blocks. Each thread claims its next block from one shared counter. The generated plugin chooses the number of helpers for each pass. The number is not fixed. In the traced runs, the number was 7 helpers at tp2. In two cases the calling thread does every store. The first case is a caller with a single worker. The handwritten plugins and the unit tests are such callers. The second case is a pass of 16 tokens or fewer.

## Passage 2

**Where write does worse than read.** Write keeps less than read in two kinds of rows. The first kind has two writers in one DSU (DynamIQ Shared Unit, the Arm block that groups several cores around a shared cache) at a size of 160 KiB. The second kind has eight writers at any size. In these rows the writers share one path. That path is limited by one of two things: the mesh port of one DSU, or the DRAM write limit (the highest rate at which the memory accepts writes) [section 8]. Each write stream carries 32 GB/s. Each read stream carries 9 to 12 GB/s. So the write streams saturate the shared path (fill it to its maximum rate) with fewer streams than the read streams do.

## Passage 3

Codex (the OpenAI coding agent) gave a final assessment. The plan now states that assessment. The rows can show four things:

- whether the gain depends on the prefetchers (the hardware units that fetch data before the core asks for it)
- whether the prefetchers send their data to the L3 (the third-level cache)
- whether demand reads (reads that the program itself issues) find their cache lines in the L3
- whether more requests wait at the home nodes

The rows alone cannot distinguish your hypothesis from the alternative. Your hypothesis is that the data is already in the L3 when the core asks for it. The alternative is that the DSU handles the same prefetch requests faster. The external-fetch count with the L3 enabled remains "Insufficient data". That status holds until a counter's source and population are established on the target. Among the proposed interventions, only the bit-6 boot acts directly on the mechanism in your hypothesis.

## Notes

**Terms I could not define (Insufficient data).** The project term list or the surrounding document would resolve them. Define each at first use if the document does not already do so.

| Passage | Terms |
|---|---|
| 1 | K rows, main helper threads, generated plugin, handwritten plugins, tp2 |
| 2 | mesh port, "keeps" (the passage does not say what quantity write keeps) |
| 3 | home nodes, external-fetch count, a counter's "source and population", bit-6 boot |

**Definitions I added from general knowledge.** Verify that each one matches the project: masked store, scatter, DSU, DRAM write limit, saturate, Codex, prefetchers, L3, demand reads.

**Word changes that affect meaning.** Confirm each one.

| Original | Rewrite | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| "write loses" | "write does worse than read" | Literal wording for the idiom. |
| "DRAM write ceiling" | "DRAM write limit" | Revert this if section 8 uses "ceiling" as its term. |
| "saturate sooner" | "saturate with fewer streams" | This is my reading of "sooner". |
| "your picture" | "your hypothesis" | Literal wording for the metaphor. |
| "aim at the L3" | "send their data to the L3" | Literal wording for the metaphor. |
| "on the table" | "proposed" | Literal wording for the idiom. |
| "with the L3 on" | "with the L3 enabled" | Literal wording. |
| three "whether" groups | four bullets | The second group held two separate claims. |
